title: Propitiation
definition: Propitiation is Christ's wrath-bearing sacrifice that satisfies God's holy justice and opens the way for mercy.
summary: Propitiation teaches that Christ's sacrifice satisfies God's righteous wrath against sin.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the sacrifice appointed by God, displaying both divine justice and saving love.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Propitiation means Christ turned away God's righteous wrath by offering Himself for sin. Scripture does not present God's anger as uncontrolled rage, but as holy opposition to evil and guilt.

At the cross, wrath is not ignored or redirected unfairly. It is satisfied in the sacrifice God Himself provides through His Son.

Jesus is the propitiation for sin. In Him, guilty sinners find mercy because justice has been answered and God's holy love has acted to save.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Propitiation matters because a Gospel without wrath cannot explain the depth of the cross. This doctrine corrects shallow views of sin and shows why the death of Christ was necessary for peace with God.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Do not treat sin lightly or God's holiness casually. Worship Christ as the One who bore wrath in your place, and proclaim the cross as the place where holy justice and saving mercy meet.
